source: 202 BC: recalled to Africa, Hannibal faces Scipio and Masinissa on the plain near Zama. The elephant lanes are prepared, the Roman camps are fortified, and the Iron Sepulcher no longer waits at the edge of history. Take all four camps and break both risings of the dead — nothing less ends this war.

source: 215-212 BC: Capua and the Campanian allies sustain Hannibal while Rome avoids another Cannae and attacks roads, farms, and loyalties. Fortify the Punic supply quarter and break all three coordinated assaults — the quarter is not held until the last consular column lies dead in the streets.

source: 216 BC: the consuls mass Rome's greatest field army beside the Aufidus. Yield the Punic center by design, win both cavalry wings, close the double envelopment, then take the principal camp, the reserve camp, and the allied camp across the river road.

source: 217 BC: Flaminius pursues along the northern shore of Lake Trasimene. Mist closes the road between lake and wooded height — and it will not hold for long. Strike the length of the column and seize both field posts within twenty minutes, before the air clears and a cohort carries word out of the basin.
translation_en_US: 217 BC: Flaminius pursues along the northern shore of Lake Trasimene. Mist closes the road between lake and wooded height — and it will not hold for long. Strike the length of the column and seize both field posts within twenty minutes, before the air clears and a cohort carries word out of the basin.

source: 218 BC: Hannibal turns from the Rhône into the Alps with soldiers, cavalry, baggage animals, and elephants. Set your builders to the slopes while the mountain peoples contest every switchback; do not follow the grave-lights into the snow.

The pass cannot be taken by the sword alone — it must be paid for in timber, stone and iron. source: 218 BC: near the Ticinus, Scipio's reconnaissance force tests Hannibal's cavalry. Win the mounted engagement, cut the bridge road, and overrun both Roman camps before their scouts carry a clean account back to the consul.

source: The tutorial is a guided first battle on a small meadow. Each step names one goal, tells you when it is done, and explains why an order is refused. Steps can be paused, skipped and replayed at any time.

It also points: the button a step is talking about lights up in the command bar, and what you are meant to act on is ringed on the field and pinned on the minimap - press Show me to swing the camera onto it. source: Wood comes from pine trees, stone from boulders and iron from ore seams. The yard's piles grow and shrink with your stores.

A builder harvests a node with Collect (or Auto Gather), then carries the load to the stone yard beside a friendly barracks. Only when it is dropped there does the counter in the top bar rise. The yard's piles grow and shrink with your stores.

source: The top-left buttons pause the battle and set the speed, from half up to quadruple; Space pauses too, and + and - step through the speeds. The active speed stays lit while paused and can be changed there. Move the camera with the arrow keys or WASD, or push the mouse to the screen edge; scroll or PgUp and PgDown to zoom, Q and E to rotate, Ctrl with the up and down arrows to tilt; Home returns to your camp and Follow keeps the camera on your selection. Every one of these can be rebound under Settings › Controls, where each camera command says what it does.
translation_en_US: The top-left buttons pause the battle and set the speed, from half up to quadruple; Space pauses too, and + and - step through the speeds. The active speed stays lit while paused and can be changed there. Move the camera with the arrow keys or WASD, or push the mouse to the screen edge; scroll or PgUp and PgDown to zoom, Q and E to rotate, Ctrl with the up and down arrows to tilt; Home returns to your camp and Follow keeps the camera on your selection. Every one of these can be rebound under Settings › Controls, where each camera command says what it does.

source: Right-click the ground to move, right-click an enemy to attack. Hold the right button and drag before releasing to choose the way the troops will face: one unit turns to face where you drag, several units are placed in formation facing it. The command grid offers Attack, Guard, Patrol, Hold, Stop and the builder and commander orders. A marker shows where troops are going and the banner above the grid confirms each order - or explains why it was refused.
translation_en_US: Right-click the ground to move, right-click an enemy to attack. Hold the right button and drag before releasing to choose the way the troops will face: one unit turns to face where you drag, several units are placed in formation facing it. The command grid offers Attack, Guard, Patrol, Hold, Stop and the builder and commander orders. A marker shows where troops are going and the banner above the grid confirms each order - or explains why it was refused.

source: Spearmen hold a line, archers punish from behind it, cavalry breaks flanks, healers mend nearby wounded on their own. Right-click and drag with several units selected to deploy them in a formation that faces the drag; the Formation order opens the same planner where they stand. Run trades stamina for speed.
translation_en_US: Spearmen hold a line, archers punish from behind it, cavalry breaks flanks, healers mend nearby wounded on their own. Right-click and drag with several units selected to deploy them in a formation that faces the drag; the Formation order opens the same planner where they stand. Run trades stamina for speed.

source: Press Guard, then left-click the ground the troops should hold. They fight anything that comes within about 10 m of that spot, let go of anything that runs past it, and walk back once the fight is over. Press Guard again, or give a move or attack order, to release them; Stop alone will not lift it. Any soldier can guard.
translation_en_US: Press Guard, then left-click the ground the troops should hold. They fight anything that comes within about 10 m of that spot, let go of anything that runs past it, and walk back once the fight is over. Press Guard again, or give a move or attack order, to release them; Stop alone will not lift it. Any soldier can guard.

source: Press Hold and the troops kneel where they stand. They never take a step, but they reach further, hit harder and take more punishment than they would on the move, and braced spears gut a cavalry charge. That is the trade: pursuit for staying power. Press Hold again, or give a move, attack or Stop order, to stand them up. Only archers and spearmen can hold.
translation_en_US: Press Hold and the troops kneel where they stand. They never take a step, but they reach further, hit harder and take more punishment than they would on the move, and braced spears gut a cavalry charge. That is the trade: pursuit for staying power. Press Hold again, or give a move, attack or Stop order, to stand them up. Only archers and spearmen can hold.

source: Press Patrol, left-click the first waypoint, then left-click the second. The troops march between the two points for good and attack whatever crosses the line - useful for watching a flank while you look elsewhere. Right-click cancels while you are setting it; any other order, or Stop, clears the route.
translation_en_US: Press Patrol, left-click the first waypoint, then left-click the second. The troops march between the two points for good and attack whatever crosses the line - useful for watching a flank while you look elsewhere. source: With the commander selected, Aura empowers his troops for a stretch and then has to recharge - each commander brings his own bonus, radius and timings, and the button prints them along with the time left. A glow marks every soldier inside the ring, the ring travels with him, and a wounded commander cannot call it. Rally plants a flag that your army marches to - useful for pulling a scattered force back into a line.
translation_en_US: With the commander selected, Aura empowers his troops for a stretch and then has to recharge - each commander brings his own bonus, radius and timings, and the button prints them along with the time left. A glow marks every soldier inside the ring, the ring travels with him, and a wounded commander cannot call it. Rally plants a flag that your army marches to - useful for pulling a scattered force back into a line.

source: A damaged building can be repaired by a builder with the Repair order. A building you no longer need can be taken down with the Dismantle order: pick your builders, press Dismantle and click the building. Part of what it cost comes back once the work is done, and calling the crew off before then pays nothing.
translation_en_US: A damaged building can be repaired by a builder with the Repair order. A building you no longer need can be taken down with the Dismantle order: pick your builders, press Dismantle and click the building. Part of what it cost comes back once the work is done, and calling the crew off before then pays nothing.

source: Food feeds your settlement: every civilian recruited at a Home costs it. A Farm grows grain in cycles; when the field turns gold a builder reaps it with Collect and hauls the grain home, and the field is sown again. Builders can also slaughter a sheep for a smaller haul. Auto Gather set to food keeps a builder working the farms.
translation_en_US: Food feeds your settlement: every civilian recruited at a Home costs it. A Farm grows grain in cycles; when the field turns gold a builder reaps it with Collect and hauls the grain home, and the field is sown again. Builders can also slaughter a sheep for a smaller haul. Auto Gather set to food keeps a builder working the farms.

source: Every card - recruit or building - lists its price. A grey card means something is short; hover it to read what. Homes cost 50 wood and 15 stone, a farm 40 wood and 10 stone, a barracks 100 wood and 60 stone, a defence tower 60 wood and 80 stone; soldiers cost wood and iron plus reserve, and civilians cost food.
translation_en_US: Every card - recruit or building - lists its price. A grey card means something is short; hover it to read what. Homes cost 50 wood and 15 stone, a farm 40 wood and 10 stone, a barracks 100 wood and 60 stone, a defence tower 60 wood and 80 stone; soldiers cost wood and iron plus reserve, and civilians cost food.

source: Barracks recruit soldiers and hold your stockpile yard. Homes raise families and civilians. Farms grow grain that builders reap for food. Defence towers shoot at anything in range. Marketplaces trade. Temples strengthen morale and take in healers. Walls and gates shape the field; gates open for your own troops.
translation_en_US: Barracks recruit soldiers and hold your stockpile yard. Homes raise families and civilians. Farms grow grain that builders reap for food. Defence towers shoot at anything in range. Marketplaces trade. Temples strengthen morale and take in healers. Walls and gates shape the field; gates open for your own troops.

source: Left-click a barracks and pick a soldier; healers take their vows at a temple instead. Recruits queue up to five deep and march out to the rally flag. Each costs reserve from the building's own pool as well as materials.
translation_en_US: Left-click a barracks and pick a soldier; healers take their vows at a temple instead. Recruits queue up to five deep and march out to the rally flag. Each costs reserve from the building's own pool as well as materials.

source: A barracks or temple starts with a reserve and spends it on every recruit; the card shows exactly what each one costs. Homes refill it: each Home raises families over time, a civilian can be recruited there for food and sent to either building with Deliver, and that building's reserve grows. A squad then stands in the field for what it cost, which is what the top bar counts against the map's manpower cap.

source: A fertile valley for two. One channel runs the whole map north to south and only two fords cross it. A cross spur on each bank means you either hug the water or swing wide to reach them, and the boomerang ridge cupping each start makes the back door terrain rather than a wall. Nothing haunts this valley: it is the plain match, with no Sepulcher to distract either side.

source: Deep wet pine forest for two. A crater wall rings the shrine bowl at the centre and no road enters it - the gates cut through its rim are the only way in, so the middle belongs to whoever will fight for it on foot. Everything else is one ring road and the trees.

source: Four camps in a snowed-in basin. Two melt races cross at its centre and cut the ground into quarters, so every neighbour is a bridge away: an inner crossing in the open, or a longer one out under the rim ranges. Four corner tarns and four barrow cairns fill the rest.
translation_en_US: Four camps in a snowed-in basin. Two melt races cross at its centre and cut the ground into quarters, so every neighbour is a bridge away: an inner crossing in the open, or a longer one out under the rim ranges. Four corner tarns and four barrow cairns fill the rest.

source: Four camps on a dry Iberian hillside. No river runs here - the terraces are the map. Each camp looks out through a horned terrace wall with a gate at either horn, and the old press mound in the middle is high ground four worn tracks climb.
translation_en_US: Four camps on a dry Iberian hillside. No river runs here - the terraces are the map. Each camp looks out through a horned terrace wall with a gate at either horn, and the old press mound in the middle is high ground four worn tracks climb.

source: Six camps in a banded rock desert. Three races cross at the middle and cut the ground into six wedges, so every neighbour is two crossings away: one under the junction knaps, one out at the rim stacks. A mesa lies across each wedge, and the lane past it is where the sector is won.
translation_en_US: Six camps in a banded rock desert. Three races cross at the middle and cut the ground into six wedges, so every neighbour is two crossings away: one under the junction knaps, one out at the rim stacks. A mesa lies across each wedge, and the lane past it is where the sector is won.

source: Three camps a side along one broad channel. The Amber runs the whole map and only three ferry crossings span it, so a bank is a front line: the highway behind each bank links its three camps, and every attack has to buy a bridge first.
translation_en_US: Three camps a side along one broad channel. The Amber runs the whole map and only three ferry crossings span it, so a bank is a front line: the highway behind each bank links its three camps, and every attack has to buy a bridge first.

source: A redoubt above a dry ford, for one. A spur of rock runs the length of the approach and the two shoulders close the flanks, so everything coming down from the north is committed to one of two lanes -- the cart gate in the west, the goat path in the east -- and they do not meet again until the ground in front of the camp. One line cannot hold both mouths, so holding here is a question of which lane you stand in and when you leave it.

A spur of rock runs the length of the approach and the two shoulders close the flanks, so everything coming down from the north is committed to one of two lanes -- the cart gate in the west, the goat path in the east -- and they do not meet again until the ground in front of the camp. One line cannot hold both mouths, so holding here is a question of which lane you stand in and when you leave it.

source: A timber detail's cut above the Pinewater, for one. The near stand beside the camp is already half felled, so the levy is only filled out of the deep pines a long haul north-east, past the spine of rock the haul road has to swing around. The scree that gives up the stone lies the other way entirely, and the crew is not big enough to work both without splitting it.

source: Final battle in Africa: blunt Scipio's line, survive the Numidian cavalry, and seize all four Roman camps while breaking both risings of the dead.
translation_en_US: Final battle in Africa: blunt Scipio's line, survive the Numidian cavalry, and seize all four Roman camps while breaking both risings of the dead.

source: Fine. Sempronius rides to Rome to explain his morning. Half a legion walked out of that water and kept walking, and they will meet you again in the spring with dry feet and long memories.
translation_en_US: Fine. Sempronius rides to Rome to explain his morning. Half a legion walked out of that water and kept walking, and they will meet you again in the spring with dry feet and long memories.

source: First battle on Italian soil. Win the cavalry duel, then seize the Roman reserve camp before fresh reinforcements regroup.
translation_en_US: First battle on Italian soil. Win the cavalry duel, then seize the Roman reserve camp before fresh reinforcements regroup.

source: Hannibal falls, and the allied towns abandon the field.
translation_en_US: Hannibal falls, and the allied towns abandon the field.

source: Hannibal's first Italian victory is a test of tempo and cavalry control. Ford-shades complicate the flanks but do not replace the Roman enemy.
translation_en_US: Hannibal's first Italian victory is a test of tempo and cavalry control. Ford-shades complicate the flanks but do not replace the Roman enemy.

source: Hannibal's masterpiece becomes a prolonged operational battle, not a single frontal collision.
translation_en_US: Hannibal's masterpiece becomes a prolonged operational battle, not a single frontal collision.

source: Hold the field, then. My horse is dead, my son is dragging me off it by the arm, and I find I can still count. You have won a ford. Italy is nine hundred miles long.
translation_en_US: Hold the field, then. My horse is dead, my son is dragging me off it by the arm, and I find I can still count. You have won a ford. Italy is nine hundred miles long.

source: Hold the river line and break all three Roman crossings. Let the cold and the water do the work Sempronius will not.
translation_en_US: Hold the river line and break all three Roman crossings. Let the cold and the water do the work Sempronius will not.

source: Hold the ruins. Force the Romans to fight on two grounds at once.
translation_en_US: Hold the ruins. Force the Romans to fight on two grounds at once.

source: Hold the southern bank through all three crossings. Sempronius spends his army on the ice; you have only to still be standing.
translation_en_US: Hold the southern bank through all three crossings. Sempronius spends his army on the ice; you have only to still be standing.

source: If the central camp falls, the Campanian alliance dies with it.
translation_en_US: If the central camp falls, the Campanian alliance dies with it.

source: It is finished. Carthage will have terms, and the terms will be her fleet burned in her own harbour where she can watch it. You were the better general. It has not turned out to matter.
translation_en_US: It is finished. Carthage will have terms, and the terms will be her fleet burned in her own harbour where she can watch it. You were the better general. It has not turned out to matter.

source: Keep Capua, then. I shall come back after the harvest, and after the one following it. I have buried three consuls who were in a hurry. Patience is cheaper, and it does not require a triumph.
translation_en_US: Keep Capua, then. I shall come back after the harvest, and after the one following it. I have buried three consuls who were in a hurry. Patience is cheaper, and it does not require a triumph.

source: Lose the river camp and the cold takes what the Romans couldn't.
translation_en_US: Lose the river camp and the cold takes what the Romans couldn't.

source: Lose the supply camp and the army starves before it reaches the snow line.
translation_en_US: Lose the supply camp and the army starves before it reaches the snow line.

source: Lose your camp and the tempo dies with it.
translation_en_US: Lose your camp and the tempo dies with it.

source: Mist on a lake road. Flaminius holds that a column moves faster than an ambush can close, and he is a consul, so he must be right. Do enjoy the next hour. I shall be the one writing the account of it.
translation_en_US: Mist on a lake road. Flaminius holds that a column moves faster than an ambush can close, and he is a consul, so he must be right. Do enjoy the next hour. I shall be the one writing the account of it.

source: No living formation remains to hold the gates.
translation_en_US: No living formation remains to hold the gates.

source: Preserve the market and four homes: Campania is being defended for its people and supplies, not merely its walls.
translation_en_US: Preserve the market and four homes: Campania is being defended for its people and supplies, not merely its walls.

source: Provision the column for the descent: harvest timber, stone and iron from the pass while the mountain tribes contest every switchback.
translation_en_US: Provision the column for the descent: harvest timber, stone and iron from the pass while the mountain tribes contest every switchback.

source: Raze every Roman post. Leave Scipio nothing to rally behind.
translation_en_US: Raze every Roman post. Leave Scipio nothing to rally behind.

source: Seal the road. Let no scout cross the Ticino alive.
translation_en_US: Seal the road. Let no scout cross the Ticino alive.

source: Seize all four Roman camps — the consular line, Masinissa's Numidians, the rear guard, and the northern camp — before the cavalry closes your rear.
translation_en_US: Seize all four Roman camps — the consular line, Masinissa's Numidians, the rear guard, and the northern camp — before the cavalry closes your rear.

source: Seize both Roman camps. The ambush is not finished until their flags come down.
translation_en_US: Seize both Roman camps. The ambush is not finished until their flags come down.

source: Seize the two river forts. Leave no crossing for Scipio's army to inherit.
translation_en_US: Seize the two river forts. Leave no crossing for Scipio's army to inherit.

source: Sixty men and a shrine the local people will not walk past after dark. My orders say investigate. I would sooner burn it and write that we investigated, but the Senate reads.
translation_en_US: Sixty men and a shrine the local people will not walk past after dark. My orders say investigate. I would sooner burn it and write that we investigated, but the Senate reads.

source: So the centre gave and the wings did not. That was well done, and I say so, and I was inside it. Rome has lost an army and a ring for every knight in it. Rome has not yet lost anything that matters.
translation_en_US: So the centre gave and the wings did not. That was well done, and I say so, and I was inside it. Rome has lost an army and a ring for every knight in it. Rome has not yet lost anything that matters.

source: So you came down the far side. Fewer, and on foot, and I am told you left the baggage up in the snow along with the men who were carrying it. Italy is waiting. Italy is not empty.
translation_en_US: So you came down the far side. Fewer, and on foot, and I am told you left the baggage up in the snow along with the men who were carrying it. Italy is waiting. Italy is not empty.

source: So you have come down out of the rocks after all. Fewer than the count they gave me, and greyer. Well. The Ticinus is shallow, the ground beyond it is ours, and I have a great deal of time in which to be wrong about you.
translation_en_US: So you have come down out of the rocks after all. Fewer than the count they gave me, and greyer. Well. The Ticinus is shallow, the ground beyond it is ours, and I have a great deal of time in which to be wrong about you.

source: So. The Barcid crawls down to the Rhone. Cross where you like - the river is not particular about whose bones it keeps, and Rome has a great deal of patience and a very great many shovels. My surveyors are already pacing out your grave. They tell me the ground here drinks well.
translation_en_US: So. The Barcid crawls down to the Rhone. Cross where you like - the river is not particular about whose bones it keeps, and Rome has a great deal of patience and a very great many shovels. My surveyors are already pacing out your grave. They tell me the ground here drinks well.

source: Spring the ambush and capture both Roman field camps within twenty minutes, before the mist lifts and a cohort escapes the basin.
translation_en_US: Spring the ambush and capture both Roman field camps within twenty minutes, before the mist lifts and a cohort escapes the basin.

source: Stand your ground. The last soldier alone is not a force — he is a sacrifice.
translation_en_US: Stand your ground. The last soldier alone is not a force — he is a sacrifice.

source: Take the bridge camp and the eastern reserve quarter before the Roman scouts vanish into the fog.
translation_en_US: Take the bridge camp and the eastern reserve quarter before the Roman scouts vanish into the fog.

source: Take the crossings, then. Take the whole cold length of the road north and every stone laid on it. Rome does not lose provinces - she lends them, at interest, and I am told the collectors on this road wear no faces at all.
translation_en_US: Take the crossings, then. Take the whole cold length of the road north and every stone laid on it. Rome does not lose provinces - she lends them, at interest, and I am told the collectors on this road wear no faces at all.

source: The Roman column walks into a geographical trap and is destroyed by converging attacks while the lakeside Sepulcher altar remains an optional horror.
translation_en_US: The Roman column walks into a geographical trap and is destroyed by converging attacks while the lakeside Sepulcher altar remains an optional horror.

source: The Romans are baited into the winter river and punished by Mago's concealed force, then the defense becomes an assault on a complete winter camp.
translation_en_US: The Romans are baited into the winter river and punished by Mago's concealed force, then the defense becomes an assault on a complete winter camp.

source: The commander falls — and every line collapses behind him.
translation_en_US: The commander falls — and every line collapses behind him.

source: The commander falls — the vigil ends. And the dead keep walking.
translation_en_US: The commander falls — the vigil ends. And the dead keep walking.

source: The crossing is a running battle against terrain, local resistance, and Roman influence. Sepulcher grave-lights remain a dangerous side path rather than the campaign's main enemy.
translation_en_US: The crossing is a running battle against terrain, local resistance, and Roman influence. Sepulcher grave-lights remain a dangerous side path rather than the campaign's main enemy.

source: The final confrontation is Carthage against three coordinated Roman commands, until an Iron Sepulcher host attacks from the battlefield's neglected flank.
translation_en_US: The final confrontation is Carthage against three coordinated Roman commands, until an Iron Sepulcher host attacks from the battlefield's neglected flank.

source: The lights are out and the ground is quiet. Count them twice and burn what will burn. Whatever was in there stood here before Rome and will stand here after it. Tonight it simply has other business.
translation_en_US: The lights are out and the ground is quiet. Count them twice and burn what will burn. Whatever was in there stood here before Rome and will stand here after it. Tonight it simply has other business.

source: The mist lifted a little early for you. It happens. The lake will keep what it has been given, and the thing beneath the altar on the shore is not particular about whose it is.
translation_en_US: The mist lifted a little early for you. It happens. The lake will keep what it has been given, and the thing beneath the altar on the shore is not particular about whose it is.

source: The pass keeps them, then. A word of advice to whoever reads this: do not follow the lights on the snowfield. Whatever carries a lantern at that height stopped being a shepherd a long time ago.
translation_en_US: The pass keeps them, then. A word of advice to whoever reads this: do not follow the lights on the snowfield. Whatever carries a lantern at that height stopped being a shepherd a long time ago.

source: The river keeps whatever it is given. Your elephants went in and not all of them came out, and the Trebia is not a large river. Rome has never needed a large one.
translation_en_US: The river keeps whatever it is given. Your elephants went in and not all of them came out, and the Trebia is not a large river. Rome has never needed a large one.

source: The scouts are not coming back, then. Well - everyone begins somewhere, and you have begun by killing eleven men who were expecting their lunch. Rome will send someone who counts next time.
translation_en_US: The scouts are not coming back, then. Well - everyone begins somewhere, and you have begun by killing eleven men who were expecting their lunch. Rome will send someone who counts next time.

source: Then it holds a little longer. Go home to your Senate and tell them what a Roman looks like from close to. I shall be here in the spring, and the spring after that, and I am younger than you.
translation_en_US: Then it holds a little longer. Go home to your Senate and tell them what a Roman looks like from close to. I shall be here in the spring, and the spring after that, and I am younger than you.

source: There. No battle, no glory, no monument: a town with nothing left in it and a road with my army standing on it. They will call me the Delayer. Let them. Your dead will not care what I am called.
translation_en_US: There. No battle, no glory, no monument: a town with nothing left in it and a road with my army standing on it. They will call me the Delayer. Let them. Your dead will not care what I am called.

source: There. Sit down in the mud with the others. They tell me the men who die on this road do not stay where they are put - that they rise about the third watch and go on marching north without their officers. Do continue. You are expected.
translation_en_US: There. Sit down in the mud with the others. They tell me the men who die on this road do not stay where they are put - that they rise about the third watch and go on marching north without their officers. Do continue. You are expected.

source: There. That is what the river was for. Have your surgeons work quickly, and tell whatever is left of your baggage train that the road home goes back up the mountain.
translation_en_US: There. That is what the river was for. Have your surgeons work quickly, and tell whatever is left of your baggage train that the road home goes back up the mountain.

source: They are getting up again. Do not look at the faces; you will know some of them. Fall back to the road, keep walking, and do not stop to bury anything. It does not stay buried here.
translation_en_US: They are getting up again. Do not look at the faces; you will know some of them. Fall back to the road, keep walking, and do not stop to bury anything. It does not stay buried here.

source: They tell me you have taken an army into the Alps in October, with elephants. I have stopped chasing you. The mountain is a more thorough officer than I am and it does not require pay.
translation_en_US: They tell me you have taken an army into the Alps in October, with elephants. I have stopped chasing you. The mountain is a more thorough officer than I am and it does not require pay.

source: Twenty minutes before the mist lifts. If a cohort clears the basin, Rome learns the shape of the trap.
translation_en_US: Twenty minutes before the mist lifts. If a cohort clears the basin, Rome learns the shape of the trap.

source: You bent us and we did not break, and that is the only sentence anyone will need. Gather your dead off the Aufidus. The river runs slow here; they will be a long time going by.
translation_en_US: You bent us and we did not break, and that is the only sentence anyone will need. Gather your dead off the Aufidus. The river runs slow here; they will be a long time going by.

source: You have a walled town, an orchard, and a very great many mouths. I have the roads. I am not going to fight you. I am going to stand between you and every granary in Campania until winter explains my position better than I can.
translation_en_US: You have a walled town, an orchard, and a very great many mouths. I have the roads. I am not going to fight you. I am going to stand between you and every granary in Campania until winter explains my position better than I can.

source: You have the river town. My congratulations - you now own three hundred mouths, two wells, and a temple whose god has lately been asking after Carthage by name. Feed them. I shall come back in the spring and count what is left.
translation_en_US: You have the river town. My congratulations - you now own three hundred mouths, two wells, and a temple whose god has lately been asking after Carthage by name. Feed them. I shall come back in the spring and count what is left.

source: You killed a consul. Good. Rome keeps forty more in cupboards in the city, and I promise you the ones still in the cupboards are worse. He will be missed - briefly, and only by his creditors.
translation_en_US: You killed a consul. Good. Rome keeps forty more in cupboards in the city, and I promise you the ones still in the cupboards are worse. He will be missed - briefly, and only by his creditors.

source: Your camp falls — the field goes with it.
translation_en_US: Your camp falls — the field goes with it.

source: Your command falls — and the wings fold inward.
translation_en_US: Your command falls — and the wings fold inward.

source: ASSAULT I: infantry from north and south; cavalry raiders and engineers on the eastern consular road.
translation_en_US: ASSAULT I: infantry from north and south; cavalry raiders and engineers on the eastern consular road.

source: ASSAULT II: the Roman horns answer one another. Rotate the reserve before all three roads close.
translation_en_US: ASSAULT II: the Roman horns answer one another. Rotate the reserve before all three roads close.

source: ASSAULT III: siege engines and veteran cohorts. Hold every gate until the twentieth minute.
translation_en_US: ASSAULT III: siege engines and veteran cohorts. Hold every gate until the twentieth minute.

source: Another Roman wave is flanking from the southeast. Rotate quickly.
translation_en_US: Another Roman wave is flanking from the southeast. Rotate quickly.

source: Counterattack now. Break them while they are split by the river.
translation_en_US: Counterattack now. Break them while they are split by the river.

source: Final ridge ahead. Break the last camp to open the descent.
translation_en_US: Final ridge ahead. Break the last camp to open the descent.

source: Fix the Roman center in place. Keep both cavalry wings active.
translation_en_US: Fix the Roman center in place. Keep both cavalry wings active.

source: Grave-lights move among the western orchards. The Iron Sepulcher is watching, but the legions remain the greater danger.
translation_en_US: Grave-lights move among the western orchards. The Iron Sepulcher is watching, but the legions remain the greater danger.

source: Hold discipline. Let the Romans commit at the ford.
translation_en_US: Hold discipline. Let the Romans commit at the ford.

source: Navigate through the maze of hills and valleys. Watch for enemy patrols!
translation_en_US: Navigate through the maze of hills and valleys. Watch for enemy patrols!

source: One minute. Spend the reserve; save the camp.
translation_en_US: One minute. Spend the reserve; save the camp.

source: Roman cavalry is attempting a breakout from the south. Intercept them.
translation_en_US: Roman cavalry is attempting a breakout from the south. Intercept them.

source: Roman cavalry screens the field. Punch through before reserves arrive.
translation_en_US: Roman cavalry screens the field. Punch through before reserves arrive.

source: Roman cavalry waves intensify. Collapse one flank before the rear guard arrives.
translation_en_US: Roman cavalry waves intensify. Collapse one flank before the rear guard arrives.

source: Roman reinforcements are approaching from the eastern road.
translation_en_US: Roman reinforcements are approaching from the eastern road.

source: Roman reserves are entering from the northern camp. Close the pocket faster.
translation_en_US: Roman reserves are entering from the northern camp. Close the pocket faster.

source: Roman reserves are moving from the western bank.
translation_en_US: Roman reserves are moving from the western bank.

source: Scipio extends the line. Keep your center steady and protect elephants from isolation.
translation_en_US: Scipio extends the line. Keep your center steady and protect elephants from isolation.

source: Second pass defenders are reinforcing. Keep the column moving.
translation_en_US: Second pass defenders are reinforcing. Keep the column moving.

source: Second-wave Roman cavalry is maneuvering for your rear. Rebalance your flanks.
translation_en_US: Second-wave Roman cavalry is maneuvering for your rear. Rebalance your flanks.

source: Strike now. Close the western route and split their line.
translation_en_US: Strike now. Close the western route and split their line.

source: Take the first pass quickly before the next ambush line assembles.
translation_en_US: Take the first pass quickly before the next ambush line assembles.

source: The Roman column enters the corridor. Wait for full commitment.
translation_en_US: The Roman column enters the corridor. Wait for full commitment.

source: The Roman villages are heavily defended. Coordinate your attacks!
translation_en_US: The Roman villages are heavily defended. Coordinate your attacks!

source: Three Roman columns have entered the consular roads. The first coordinated assault arrives at 17:00.
translation_en_US: Three Roman columns have entered the consular roads. The first coordinated assault arrives at 17:00.

source: Two bridges cross the Rhône. Choose your path wisely - you may need both routes!
translation_en_US: Two bridges cross the Rhône. Choose your path wisely - you may need both routes!

source: A camp is taken by standing in it, not by levelling it. Nine men cannot kill thirty-eight, but they can hold two gate yards long enough to claim them - and a Roman column without its commander stops being a column.
translation_en_US: A camp is taken by standing in it, not by levelling it. Nine men cannot kill thirty-eight, but they can hold two gate yards long enough to claim them - and a Roman column without its commander stops being a column.

source: A nation stands on its commander. Kill him and the camps go quiet and unclaimed - which, against a twenty-minute clock, is the only version of this battle that finishes in time.
translation_en_US: A nation stands on its commander. Kill him and the camps go quiet and unclaimed - which, against a twenty-minute clock, is the only version of this battle that finishes in time.

source: An assault walks toward your camp but turns for whatever it can see. Bait it with something visible and it will take the ground you chose instead of the ground it wanted.
translation_en_US: An assault walks toward your camp but turns for whatever it can see. Bait it with something visible and it will take the ground you chose instead of the ground it wanted.

source: High ground doubles a bowman and hardens him against what shoots back. The ridge over the Roman camp is worth more than the extra squadron you would have spent the same minutes recruiting.
translation_en_US: High ground doubles a bowman and hardens him against what shoots back. The ridge over the Roman camp is worth more than the extra squadron you would have spent the same minutes recruiting.

source: Iron bells answer beneath the south-western crossing. The Sepulcher is advancing on Carthage as well as Rome.
translation_en_US: Iron bells answer beneath the south-western crossing. The Sepulcher is advancing on Carthage as well as Rome.

source: Kill every enemy commander. A nation dies with the man who leads it: its camps fall neutral, its works come down and its troops leave the field.
translation_en_US: Kill every enemy commander. A nation dies with the man who leads it: its camps fall neutral, its works come down and its troops leave the field.

source: Masinissa's Numidian horse is entering from the north-eastern road.
translation_en_US: Masinissa's Numidian horse is entering from the north-eastern road.

source: Nothing new is taught here. The ridge, the bait and the beheading are all things you already know; Cannae only asks whether you can run three of them at once against four times your number.
translation_en_US: Nothing new is taught here. The ridge, the bait and the beheading are all things you already know; Cannae only asks whether you can run three of them at once against four times your number.

source: Rear guard deployment detected across the southern wadi. This is the final phase.
translation_en_US: Rear guard deployment detected across the southern wadi. This is the final phase.

source: Supply is a target - and it cuts both ways. Your market and your homes are what the Romans are actually marching at, and their siege camp keeps its own stockpile within reach of a raid.
translation_en_US: Supply is a target - and it cuts both ways. Your market and your homes are what the Romans are actually marching at, and their siege camp keeps its own stockpile within reach of a raid.

source: The shrines you have walked past all campaign were never scenery. Zama reads back over every map behind it - and the Sepulcher has no commander to kill, so the one rule that has served you since Trasimene is the one rule that will not work here.
translation_en_US: The shrines you have walked past all campaign were never scenery. Zama reads back over every map behind it - and the Sepulcher has no commander to kill, so the one rule that has served you since Trasimene is the one rule that will not work here.

source: Timber only counts once a builder unloads it at the camp. The richest stands are the furthest from the stockpile, so the mission is won on the length of the walk, not the swing of the axe.
translation_en_US: Timber only counts once a builder unloads it at the camp. The richest stands are the furthest from the stockpile, so the mission is won on the length of the walk, not the swing of the axe.

source: A guided first field, paced by the player rather than the clock: the Roman raid waits until the recruit's army stands, and the enemy camp is small enough to fall to a first attack.
translation_en_US: A guided first field, paced by the player rather than the clock: the Roman raid waits until the recruit's army stands, and the enemy camp is small enough to fall to a first attack.

source: Every system a first match asks for, in the order a new commander meets them: selection and orders, the resource loop from tree to yard, construction cost and placement, recruitment and the population that limits it, stances, the commander's aura and rally, camera, speed and objectives - then one small assault to put it all together.
translation_en_US: Every system a first match asks for, in the order a new commander meets them: selection and orders, the resource loop from tree to yard, construction cost and placement, recruitment and the population that limits it, stances, the commander's aura and rally, camera, speed and objectives - then one small assault to put it all together.

source: Kill the Roman commander and take the outpost. A nation dies with the man who leads it.
translation_en_US: Kill the Roman commander and take the outpost. A nation dies with the man who leads it.

source: Learn to command before Rome comes looking for you: select and move troops, drive off a scouting party, put builders to work on timber, stone and ore, raise a Home, recruit an army, break a Roman raid, and take the enemy camp.
translation_en_US: Learn to command before Rome comes looking for you: select and move troops, drive off a scouting party, put builders to work on timber, stone and ore, raise a Home, recruit an army, break a Roman raid, and take the enemy camp.

source: Your commander falls - and every line collapses behind him.
translation_en_US: Your commander falls - and every line collapses behind him.

source: A camp is taken by holding its yard, not by levelling it.
translation_en_US: A camp is taken by holding its yard, not by levelling it.

source: A column without its commander stops being a column.
translation_en_US: A column without its commander stops being a column.

source: Break the chiefs contesting the descent.
translation_en_US: Break the chiefs contesting the descent.

source: Break the consular line at its centre.
translation_en_US: Break the consular line at its centre.

source: Break the siege camp once the assaults are spent.
translation_en_US: Break the siege camp once the assaults are spent.

source: Bring the column to the first pass
translation_en_US: Bring the column to the first pass

source: Bring the column to the pontoon bridge on the near bank.
translation_en_US: Bring the column to the pontoon bridge on the near bank.

source: Cavalry reaches it first; hold the yard until the standard changes.
translation_en_US: Cavalry reaches it first; hold the yard until the standard changes.

source: Close the encirclement on the Aufidus camp to the north.
translation_en_US: Close the encirclement on the Aufidus camp to the north.

source: Close the trap on the column town
translation_en_US: Close the trap on the column town

source: Cut the stores for the road
translation_en_US: Cut the stores for the road

source: End the war with the men who lead it.
translation_en_US: End the war with the men who lead it.

source: Enemy camps fall neutral once their commander is dead.
translation_en_US: Enemy camps fall neutral once their commander is dead.

source: Finish the consular officers on the field.
translation_en_US: Finish the consular officers on the field.

source: Finish the officers inside the ring.
translation_en_US: Finish the officers inside the ring.

source: Flaminius must not leave the shore.
translation_en_US: Flaminius must not leave the shore.

source: Follow the valley floor east; the mountain peoples hold the switchbacks above.
translation_en_US: Follow the valley floor east; the mountain peoples hold the switchbacks above.

source: Hold the Punic quarter through every consular column.
translation_en_US: Hold the Punic quarter through every consular column.

source: Hold the gate yard of Scipio's forward town.
translation_en_US: Hold the gate yard of Scipio's forward town.

source: Hold the southern bank through every Roman assault phase.
translation_en_US: Hold the southern bank through every Roman assault phase.

source: It is the closest camp to your hill; take it before the wings close.
translation_en_US: It is the closest camp to your hill; take it before the wings close.

source: It is the closest of the four camps to your line.
translation_en_US: It is the closest of the four camps to your line.

source: Move the army up to the lower pass camp before the snow closes it.
translation_en_US: Move the army up to the lower pass camp before the snow closes it.

source: Nothing on the shore road survives once both ends are held.
translation_en_US: Nothing on the shore road survives once both ends are held.

source: Ride down the commanders once the crossings break.
translation_en_US: Ride down the commanders once the crossings break.

source: Scipio inherits any crossing you leave behind.
translation_en_US: Scipio inherits any crossing you leave behind.

source: Seize Masinissa's camp to finish the four.
translation_en_US: Seize Masinissa's camp to finish the four.

source: Seize Varro's town at the centre of the Roman line.
translation_en_US: Seize Varro's town at the centre of the Roman line.

source: Seize the camp guarding Scipio's rear.
translation_en_US: Seize the camp guarding Scipio's rear.

source: Seize the second Roman camp on the north-east road.
translation_en_US: Seize the second Roman camp on the north-east road.

source: Seize the second camp at the eastern end of the lake.
translation_en_US: Seize the second camp at the eastern end of the lake.

source: Sempronius spends his army on the ice; you only have to still be standing.
translation_en_US: Sempronius spends his army on the ice; you only have to still be standing.

source: Set builders on the slopes; the pass is paid for in materials, not blood.
translation_en_US: Set builders on the slopes; the pass is paid for in materials, not blood.

source: Stand in the gate yard of the northern advance camp until it falls to Carthage.
translation_en_US: Stand in the gate yard of the northern advance camp until it falls to Carthage.

translation_en_US: Everything starts with a selection. Left-click a soldier to select it, or hold the left button and drag a box around several. Selected troops show a ring at their feet, and the panel at the bottom lists who is under your command.

source: With troops selected, right-click on the ground to march there. A marker appears where they are headed and the banner above the command grid confirms the order. A rejected order says why it could not be carried out - read the banner when nothing happens.
translation_en_US: With troops selected, right-click on the ground to march there. A marker appears where they are headed and the banner above the command grid confirms the order. A rejected order says why it could not be carried out - read the banner when nothing happens.

source: A Roman scouting party stands just beyond your tents; the minimap marks enemies in red. Right-click an enemy to attack it, or press Attack and click the target. While your troops fight, the target panel above the command grid tracks the enemy's health.
translation_en_US: A Roman scouting party stands just beyond your tents; the minimap marks enemies in red. Right-click an enemy to attack it, or press Attack and click the target. While your troops fight, the target panel above the command grid tracks the enemy's health.

source: Wood pays for nearly everything. Select a builder, press Collect and click a pine tree. The builder fells it, carries the logs to the stone yard beside your barracks, and only when the load is dropped there does the wood counter in the top bar rise. Auto Gather keeps a builder working the nearest nodes on its own.
translation_en_US: Wood pays for nearly everything. Select a builder, press Collect and click a pine tree. The builder fells it, carries the logs to the stone yard beside your barracks, and only when the load is dropped there does the wood counter in the top bar rise. Auto Gather keeps a builder working the nearest nodes on its own.

source: Boulders yield stone for buildings and towers; ore seams yield iron for blades and armour. Both are hauled to the same barracks yard, which fills up as your stores grow. Gold comes with the camp and from trade at a marketplace. Set one builder on the boulders and another on the ore.
translation_en_US: Boulders yield stone for buildings and towers; ore seams yield iron for blades and armour. Both are hauled to the same barracks yard, which fills up as your stores grow. Gold comes with the camp and from trade at a marketplace. Set one builder on the boulders and another on the ore.

source: Select a builder and press Build to open the structure list. Each card shows its cost in wood, stone and gold; a grey card means you cannot afford it yet. Choose Home, then move the outline: green means the ground is flat and clear, red means it is blocked. Scroll to rotate, left-click to confirm. Homes raise the families your barracks will later recruit from.
translation_en_US: Select a builder and press Build to open the structure list. Each card shows its cost in wood, stone and gold; a grey card means you cannot afford it yet. Choose Home, then move the outline: green means the ground is flat and clear, red means it is blocked. Scroll to rotate, left-click to confirm. Homes raise the families your barracks will later recruit from.

source: Left-click your barracks and pick a soldier from the production panel. Every recruit costs population and resources: the population comes from the barracks' own pool, shown on the card, and refills when civilians from your Homes are delivered to it. The bar in the top panel shows your army against the map's population cap.
translation_en_US: Left-click your barracks and pick a soldier from the production panel. Every recruit costs population and resources: the population comes from the barracks' own pool, shown on the card, and refills when civilians from your Homes are delivered to it. The bar in the top panel shows your army against the map's population cap.

source: One soldier is not an army. Keep recruiting until you field eight - mix spearmen to hold a line with archers to punish whatever charges it. If a card turns grey, the tutorial hint tells you what ran short. New recruits gather at the barracks' rally flag; set one from the production panel.
translation_en_US: One soldier is not an army. Keep recruiting until you field eight - mix spearmen to hold a line with archers to punish whatever charges it. If a card turns grey, the tutorial hint tells you what ran short. New recruits gather at the barracks' rally flag; set one from the production panel.

source: A Roman raid is coming. The wave tracker counts it down and the minimap marks its entry point. Form up near your barracks: spearmen in front, archers behind, and the commander close so his aura reaches them. Break the raid to continue.
translation_en_US: A Roman raid is coming. The wave tracker counts it down and the minimap marks its entry point. Form up near your barracks: spearmen in front, archers behind, and the commander close so his aura reaches them. Break the raid to continue.

source: Move the view with the arrow keys or WASD, or push the mouse to the screen edge. Scroll to zoom, Q and E rotate, Ctrl with the up and down arrows tilts, and Home returns to your camp. Follow keeps the camera on your selection. Move the camera now.
translation_en_US: Move the view with the arrow keys or WASD, or push the mouse to the screen edge. Scroll to zoom, Q and E rotate, Ctrl with the up and down arrows tilts, and Home returns to your camp. Follow keeps the camera on your selection. Move the camera now.

source: The top-left buttons pause the battle and set the speed, from half up to quadruple. Space pauses too, and + and - step through the speeds without reaching for the bar. The active speed stays lit while paused, and you can change it there. Change the speed or pause and resume now.
translation_en_US: The top-left buttons pause the battle and set the speed, from half up to quadruple. Space pauses too, and + and - step through the speeds without reaching for the bar. The active speed stays lit while paused, and you can change it there. Change the speed or pause and resume now.

source: The star in the top bar shows your current objective. Press Escape and choose Objectives to read the full briefing: what wins the mission, what loses it, and any optional goals. Open it now, then return to the battle.
translation_en_US: The star in the top bar shows your current objective. Press Escape and choose Objectives to read the full briefing: what wins the mission, what loses it, and any optional goals. Open it now, then return to the battle.

source: You know everything the field will ask of you. The Roman camp lies across the meadow. Gather your army, keep the commander behind the line, and take the camp: kill the Roman commander and the mission is won.
translation_en_US: You know everything the field will ask of you. The Roman camp lies across the meadow. Gather your army, keep the commander behind the line, and take the camp: kill the Roman commander and the mission is won.

source: Soldiers can be told how to behave, and the three orders are not the same. Guard: click a spot; they meet anything that comes near it, then walk back to it. Hold: they never take a step, but they reach further, hit harder and brace against a charge - archers and spearmen only. Patrol: click two waypoints and they march the beat between them, fighting whatever crosses it. Hover any of the three to read the full rules, then give one of them to your soldiers.
translation_en_US: Soldiers can be told how to behave, and the three orders are not the same. Guard: click a spot; they meet anything that comes near it, then walk back to it. Hold: they never take a step, but they reach further, hit harder and brace against a charge - archers and spearmen only. Patrol: click two waypoints and they march the beat between them, fighting whatever crosses it. Hover any of the three to read the full rules, then give one of them to your soldiers.

source: Your commander carries the standard. Troops near him fight with higher morale, and while he is selected two commands appear: Aura empowers every soldier in a ring around him for a stretch and then recharges - the button prints the radius, how long it lasts and how long until it returns - and Rally plants a flag that the army marches to. If he dies, your lines break and the mission is lost - keep him behind the spears. Trigger the Aura now.
translation_en_US: Your commander carries the standard. Troops near him fight with higher morale, and while he is selected two commands appear: Aura empowers every soldier in a ring around him for a stretch and then recharges - the button prints the radius, how long it lasts and how long until it returns - and Rally plants a flag that the army marches to. If he dies, your lines break and the mission is lost - keep him behind the spears. Trigger the Aura now.

source: An ancient army marched with its own carpenters and masons, raising and fortifying a camp every night.
translation_en_US: An ancient army marched with its own carpenters and masons, raising and fortifying a camp every night.

source: Ancient armies kept surgeons close to the line; the wounded who walked away were the difference between a campaign and a rout.
translation_en_US: Ancient armies kept surgeons close to the line; the wounded who walked away were the difference between a campaign and a rout.

source: Archers are the answer to it, and massed bows bring it down before it closes.
translation_en_US: Archers are the answer to it, and massed bows bring it down before it closes.

source: As brittle as any archer, and it withers as soon as the line in front of it fails.
translation_en_US: As brittle as any archer, and it withers as soon as the line in front of it fails.

source: Behind every field army stood the farms and quarries that fed it, and the people who worked them.
translation_en_US: Behind every field army stood the farms and quarries that fed it, and the people who worked them.

source: Bows decided few ancient battles outright, but a volley loosed before contact could break a formation's nerve.
translation_en_US: Bows decided few ancient battles outright, but a volley loosed before contact could break a formation's nerve.

source: Breaks on a braced spear line, which cuts mounted troops down at more than twice the usual rate.
translation_en_US: Breaks on a braced spear line, which cuts mounted troops down at more than twice the usual rate.

source: Cannot fight. Left unguarded it dies to anything that reaches it.
translation_en_US: Cannot fight. Left unguarded it dies to anything that reaches it.

source: Carries more health than any squad on the field, and its reach breaks a line that stands to receive it.
translation_en_US: Carries more health than any squad on the field, and its reach breaks a line that stands to receive it.

source: Carthage bought its archers from Libya and the islands, paying in silver what Rome demanded of its citizens.
translation_en_US: Carthage bought its archers from Libya and the islands, paying in silver what Rome demanded of its citizens.

source: Carthage sent its own citizens into the line only when the city itself was threatened. The rest of the army was hired.
translation_en_US: Carthage sent its own citizens into the line only when the city itself was threatened. The rest of the army was hired.

source: Carthage took its elephants from the forests south of the Atlas, smaller than the Indian beasts but the terror of Italy.
translation_en_US: Carthage took its elephants from the forests south of the Atlas, smaller than the Indian beasts but the terror of Italy.

source: Carthaginian engineers learned artillery from the Greek cities of Sicily, and then improved on it.
translation_en_US: Carthaginian engineers learned artillery from the Greek cities of Sicily, and then improved on it.

source: Cavalry rarely charged an unbroken line. It waited for a flank to open and then finished the day.
translation_en_US: Cavalry rarely charged an unbroken line. It waited for a flank to open and then finished the day.

source: Close-order swordsmen were the expensive core of a Mediterranean army, drilled to hold a line rather than to duel.
translation_en_US: Close-order swordsmen were the expensive core of a Mediterranean army, drilled to hold a line rather than to duel.

source: Costs nothing to raise and never breaks, so it buys time no living troop would.
translation_en_US: Costs nothing to raise and never breaks, so it buys time no living troop would.

source: Defenceless at close quarters. Infantry that reaches it kills it in a few seconds.
translation_en_US: Defenceless at close quarters. Infantry that reaches it kills it in a few seconds.

source: Denies ground nothing else can reach, at well over twice an archer's range.
translation_en_US: Denies ground nothing else can reach, at well over twice an archer's range.

source: Every arrow that lands leaves a curse on its target, draining the will of the formation it struck.
translation_en_US: Every arrow that lands leaves a curse on its target, draining the will of the formation it struck.

source: Fast enough to choose its own fight, and it rides down archers left without a screen.
translation_en_US: Fast enough to choose its own fight, and it rides down archers left without a screen.

source: Fragile once contacted. Cavalry overruns it whenever it has no melee screen.
translation_en_US: Fragile once contacted. Cavalry overruns it whenever it has no melee screen.

source: Gathers and delivers the resources every other unit is paid for with.
translation_en_US: Gathers and delivers the resources every other unit is paid for with.

source: Has no melee worth the name, and spears punish it the moment it is caught.
translation_en_US: Has no melee worth the name, and spears punish it the moment it is caught.

source: Horse archers came from the steppe and the desert margins, and Mediterranean armies hired them rather than raised them.
translation_en_US: Horse archers came from the steppe and the desert margins, and Mediterranean armies hired them rather than raised them.

source: Hurls fire that bursts across a formation and clings to the ground where it lands.
translation_en_US: Hurls fire that bursts across a formation and clings to the ground where it lands.

source: Hurls fire that bursts across a formation and leaves the ground burning where it lands.
translation_en_US: Hurls fire that bursts across a formation and leaves the ground burning where it lands.

source: Its arrows carry a curse that drains the will of everything they strike.
translation_en_US: Its arrows carry a curse that drains the will of everything they strike.

source: Its quiver was buried with it, and the curse worked into the shafts outlasted the hand that drew the bow.
translation_en_US: Its quiver was buried with it, and the curse worked into the shafts outlasted the hand that drew the bow.

source: Loses the straight infantry fight to swords, and caught in the open it is only a slower line.
translation_en_US: Loses the straight infantry fight to swords, and caught in the open it is only a slower line.

source: Mends nearby wounded without being told to, so a line that holds keeps its strength.
translation_en_US: Mends nearby wounded without being told to, so a line that holds keeps its strength.

source: Not a soldier. It cannot hold ground and should never be the last thing guarding a camp.
translation_en_US: Not a soldier. It cannot hold ground and should never be the last thing guarding a camp.

source: One slow body, helpless in melee, and it needs the awakened dead between it and the enemy.
translation_en_US: One slow body, helpless in melee, and it needs the awakened dead between it and the enemy.

source: Out-trades everything at range, and massed bows are the answer to a war elephant.
translation_en_US: Out-trades everything at range, and massed bows are the answer to a war elephant.

source: Outranges troops on foot and can withdraw from any fight it cannot win.
translation_en_US: Outranges troops on foot and can withdraw from any fight it cannot win.

source: Overrun in seconds by any infantry that reaches it, and far too slow to withdraw.
translation_en_US: Overrun in seconds by any infantry that reaches it, and far too slow to withdraw.

source: Phoenician craftsmen raised the harbours and walls that made Carthage the richest city in the western sea.
translation_en_US: Phoenician craftsmen raised the harbours and walls that made Carthage the richest city in the western sea.

source: Raised from the burial ranks of an army that was interred still holding its shields.
translation_en_US: Raised from the burial ranks of an army that was interred still holding its shields.

source: Raises every building an army needs and repairs what the enemy breaks.
translation_en_US: Raises every building an army needs and repairs what the enemy breaks.

source: Repays its cost against cavalry, and braced on high ground it holds against far heavier attacks.
translation_en_US: Repays its cost against cavalry, and braced on high ground it holds against far heavier attacks.

source: Rome raised few archers of its own and drew them from Crete and the eastern allies instead.
translation_en_US: Rome raised few archers of its own and drew them from Crete and the eastern allies instead.

source: Rome standardised the bolt thrower until every legion carried its own, mounted on carts and served by trained crews.
translation_en_US: Rome standardised the bolt thrower until every legion carried its own, mounted on carts and served by trained crews.

source: Slower and weaker than the living line it imitates, and nothing in the field can mend it.
translation_en_US: Slower and weaker than the living line it imitates, and nothing in the field can mend it.

source: Still cavalry. A braced spear line stops it, and it cannot trade with archers at range.
translation_en_US: Still cavalry. A braced spear line stops it, and it cannot trade with archers at range.

source: The Liby-Phoenician spear was the steady centre that a mercenary army could be built around.
translation_en_US: The Liby-Phoenician spear was the steady centre that a mercenary army could be built around.

source: The Numidians rode without bridles and were the finest light horse in the Mediterranean. Rome's worst day, at Cannae, was their work.
translation_en_US: The Numidians rode without bridles and were the finest light horse in the Mediterranean. Rome's worst day, at Cannae, was their work.

source: The Sacred Band kept physicians of its own, an honour reserved for the citizen elite.
translation_en_US: The Sacred Band kept physicians of its own, an honour reserved for the citizen elite.

source: The bolt thrower was the accurate half of a siege train, used against men and gates alike.
translation_en_US: The bolt thrower was the accurate half of a siege train, used against men and gates alike.

source: The bolt throwers of Carthage were built in the same yards as its fleet, by the same shipwrights.
translation_en_US: The bolt throwers of Carthage were built in the same yards as its fleet, by the same shipwrights.

source: The equites were drawn from the wealthiest citizens, and Rome's cavalry was never the equal of its infantry.
translation_en_US: The equites were drawn from the wealthiest citizens, and Rome's cavalry was never the equal of its infantry.

source: The fabri built the roads, the bridges and the fortified camp that went up every single night of a march.
translation_en_US: The fabri built the roads, the bridges and the fortified camp that went up every single night of a march.

source: The legionary's short sword and heavy javelin were built for one thing: closing the last twenty paces and winning there.
translation_en_US: The legionary's short sword and heavy javelin were built for one thing: closing the last twenty paces and winning there.

source: The longest reach in any army, and quick enough to loose again before its target closes.
translation_en_US: The longest reach in any army, and quick enough to loose again before its target closes.

source: The longest reach of any mounted troop, striking before the enemy line can answer.
translation_en_US: The longest reach of any mounted troop, striking before the enemy line can answer.

source: The medicus marched with the legion, and Roman field medicine was the best organised in the ancient world.
translation_en_US: The medicus marched with the legion, and Roman field medicine was the best organised in the ancient world.

source: The mounted lance traded the sword's flexibility for reach, striking before an enemy could bring a weapon to bear.
translation_en_US: The mounted lance traded the sword's flexibility for reach, striking before an enemy could bring a weapon to bear.

source: The onager kicked like the wild ass it was named for, and was Rome's answer to a wall that would not fall.
translation_en_US: The onager kicked like the wild ass it was named for, and was Rome's answer to a wall that would not fall.

source: The priests who sealed the tombs learned to open them, and now walk ahead of what they woke.
translation_en_US: The priests who sealed the tombs learned to open them, and now walk ahead of what they woke.

source: The slowest troops in the line, and they take losses crossing open ground under archery.
translation_en_US: The slowest troops in the line, and they take losses crossing open ground under archery.

source: The spear was the cheapest way to make a horse refuse a charge, and every ancient army kept a wall of them.
translation_en_US: The spear was the cheapest way to make a horse refuse a charge, and every ancient army kept a wall of them.

source: The triarii were the oldest and steadiest men in the legion, knelt behind the line and committed only when the day was in doubt.
translation_en_US: The triarii were the oldest and steadiest men in the legion, knelt behind the line and committed only when the day was in doubt.

source: The weakest body on the field. Anything that finds it kills it.
translation_en_US: The weakest body on the field. Anything that finds it kills it.

source: Torsion artillery was built on the spot from local timber and abandoned when the army moved on.
translation_en_US: Torsion artillery was built on the spot from local timber and abandoned when the army moved on.

source: War elephants terrified armies that had never met them, and were nearly useless against those that had.
translation_en_US: War elephants terrified armies that had never met them, and were nearly useless against those that had.

source: Wins the straight infantry fight against spears, and overruns unescorted siege in seconds.
translation_en_US: Wins the straight infantry fight against spears, and overruns unescorted siege in seconds.

source: Wolves are moving on the valley.
translation_en_US: Wolves are moving on the valley.

translation_en_US:
Failed to initialize OpenGL renderer.

This usually means:
1. Graphics drivers don't support required OpenGL 3.3 Core Profile
2. Running in a VM with incomplete OpenGL support
3. Qt software OpenGL fallback is unavailable or failed to initialize

To fix:
- Run run_debug_softwaregl.cmd or set QT_OPENGL=software
- Update graphics drivers
- On VMs: Enable 3D acceleration in VM settings
